samples.summary: Paste-propagated merges bypass the freeze-pane guard that `canMergeSelection` enforces and that the design doc states as an invariant
samples.evidence: The only place the "a merge may not cross a freeze pane boundary" rule is enforced is `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4414-4422: `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols` -> `return false`), and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:247 records it as a model invariant ("Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed."). The new paste path re-creates copied blocks at an arbitrary destination via `await this.store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span)` (sheet.ts:2337) with no frozen check, so copying a merged block inside the frozen region and pasting it straddling `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` produces a block the merge UI would have refused. The renderer consumes merges per frozen quadrant (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:204 `buildMergeRenderData`, 884-895 anchor/extent intersection per visible range), which assumes blocks live in one quadrant. Note `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2533) already has the same hole, so the fix likely belongs in a shared helper used by both, or by adding the frozen check to the paste refusal at sheet.ts:2286.

samples.summary: Copy/cut buffer (and marching ants) is now left up after a paste that failed for reasons unrelated to merges — notably a paste into a pivot tab or with an empty clipboard
samples.evidence: `Sheet.paste` returns `false` not only on a merge refusal but also for `if (this.pivotDefinition) return false;` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2172) and for `else { return false; }` when neither text nor html is present (sheet.ts:2246-2248). Both view call sites now gate the cleanup on the return value — packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:717-719 and packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4901-4903 — where previously `clearCopyBuffer()` ran unconditionally. So attempting a paste on a pivot tab, or with nothing on the clipboard, leaves `copyBuffer`/`isCutMode()` set (read at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5557 for the marching-ants overlay), i.e. the cut marquee stays visible after an action that can never succeed on that tab.

samples.summary: Adding a file-level `@vitest-environment jsdom` docblock switches the environment for every existing suite in merge.test.ts, not just the new HTML-paste case
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:1-3 adds `@vitest-environment jsdom` at the top of the file, which applies to the pre-existing `Sheet merge + structural edits` (line ~9) and `Sheet merge + drag-move` (line ~374) suites as well. Only the new `should refuse an HTML paste offset onto a covered cell` case needs DOMParser; the rest now run under a different (slower, DOM-globals-present) environment than the other model tests in packages/sheets/test/sheet/, which can mask node-vs-DOM assumptions in model code. Scoping the jsdom environment to the HTML case (or moving it into clipboard/html tests) keeps the other suites' environment unchanged.

finding.summary: Paste-propagated merges bypass the freeze-pane guard that `canMergeSelection` enforces and that the design doc states as an invariant
finding.evidence: The only place the "a merge may not cross a freeze pane boundary" rule is enforced is `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4414-4422: `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols` -> `return false`), and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:247 records it as a model invariant ("Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed."). The new paste path re-creates copied blocks at an arbitrary destination via `await this.store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span)` (sheet.ts:2337) with no frozen check, so copying a merged block inside the frozen region and pasting it straddling `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` produces a block the merge UI would have refused. The renderer consumes merges per frozen quadrant (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:204 `buildMergeRenderData`, 884-895 anchor/extent intersection per visible range), which assumes blocks live in one quadrant. Note `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2533) already has the same hole, so the fix likely belongs in a shared helper used by both, or by adding the frozen check to the paste refusal at sheet.ts:2286.

verdict.reason: Independently verified every claimed location. The freeze-pane merge rule is enforced only in `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4414-4422, gating `mergeSelection` at 4441); a repo-wide grep for `frozenRows|frozenCols` in sheet.ts shows no frozen check on the paste path. The internal-paste branch translates live source merges by delta (sheet.ts:2204-2224) and unconditionally writes them with `store.setMerge` (sheet.ts:2336-2344); the only paste refusals (2216, 2286) test partial overlap, not freeze boundaries. So copying a merged block in the frozen region and pasting it straddling `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` creates a block the merge UI refuses, violating the documented model invariant (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:247). Downstream consumers assume one-quadrant blocks: gridcanvas builds a single merge map (gridcanvas.ts:204, 1891-1912) then renders per frozen quadrant with clipped ranges (205) and computes block rects from anchor+span against one quadrant's scroll (toCellRect, 1917-1940); overlay.ts:194/1216 uses the same shape. In-lane for blast radius (violated invariant other modules assume, reachable from new paste code); no guard elsewhere makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: Swapping the removed loop-based `gridRange` for the shared `rangeOf` helper puts a spread-argument limit on every paste: `rangeOf` does `Math.min(...rows)`, which throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` once the pasted grid exceeds ~100k cells. `selectPastedRange` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2389) calls it unconditionally after the write has already committed, so a large paste would mutate the store and then throw out of `Sheet.paste`; the view callers only `console.error` (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4906, packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:722), leaving the grid written but unrendered and the selection stale. The deleted `gridRange` iterated with a for-loop and had no such limit. Fix belongs in `rangeOf` (make it a loop) rather than in the new call sites.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27 `rangeOf` uses `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)`; called from packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2389 for every successful paste, with no cell-count cap anywhere on the paste path (no MAX_* limit found in packages/sheets/src/model/core).

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise is factually absent from the code. `rangeOf` at packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:24-46 accumulates bounds with an explicit `for (const sref of grid.keys())` loop and scalar comparisons (`if (ref.r < minR) minR = ref.r;`), with no spread call anywhere. The only occurrence of the quoted `Math.min(...rows)` text in the file is at line 18, inside the doc comment, which states the exact opposite of the finding: the loop was chosen precisely "rather than with `Math.min(...rows)`" because "spreading a large paste's worth of them as arguments overflows the call stack (`RangeError` past ~100k cells)". The reviewer quoted the cautionary comment as if it were the implementation. A repo-wide grep of packages/sheets/src for spread `Math.min(...`/`Math.max(...)` finds hits only in formula/functions-database.ts, functions-math.ts and functions-lookup.ts — none on the paste path — and there is no second definition of `rangeOf`. The cited call site packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2389 does invoke `rangeOf` post-commit, but it is preceded by `if (grid.size === 0) return;` at line 2388, which satisfies the only precondition `rangeOf` actually has (the empty-grid throw at lines 25-27). Therefore the described failure mode — a stack-overflow RangeError thrown after the store mutation, leaving the grid written but unrendered with stale selection — cannot arise, and the proposed fix ("make `rangeOf` a loop") is already the shipped implementation.

finding.summary: `copyBuffer.merges` is a snapshot never invalidated by the other operations that mutate `this.merges`, so a later paste can re-create a block that no longer exists and silently clear destination cells under it
finding.evidence: `copy()`/`cut()` now snapshot `getMergesIntersecting(range)` into `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2153, 2173). Nothing invalidates that snapshot: `shiftCells` rewrites the merge map at sheet.ts:1320 (insert/delete rows/cols), `moveRows/moveColumns` at sheet.ts:1509, and `unmergeSelection` deletes blocks at sheet.ts:4540-4542 — none of them touch `copyBuffer` (`clearCopyBuffer` is only called from the views, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4900/5071 and spreadsheet.ts:716). So: copy a merged range, unmerge it (or insert a row above it), then paste the still-matching clipboard text — `pastedMerges` re-creates the stale block at the destination and `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:927) deletes the destination cells it now covers. Previously the stale buffer could only mis-relocate formulas; it can now delete cell content and create merge geometry that never existed.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually absent from this repository: there is no merge snapshot in `copyBuffer` to become stale. `copyBuffer`'s declared shape (sheet.ts:334-340) contains only `sourceRange, grid, rangeStyles, text, isCut` — no `merges`. `copy()` (sheet.ts:2138) and `cut()` (sheet.ts:2151) assign exactly those five fields and never call `getMergesIntersecting`; the cited lines 2153/2173 are `cut()`'s closing brace and the `pivotDefinition` early return in `paste()`. The counterexample to the absence claim is the live read at sheet.ts:2204, `const copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange);`, preceded by an explicit comment (sheet.ts:2201-2203) naming the exact hazard: 'Read the source layout live rather than snapshotting it at copy time: a snapshot survives shiftCells, moveRows/moveColumns and unmergeSelection, and would re-create a block that no longer exists.' `getMergesIntersecting` (sheet.ts:888-900) iterates `this.merges` directly, so after `unmergeSelection` or a row/column shift the paste observes the current map; `pastedMerges` (sheet.ts:2221-2224) derives from it, so a deleted block yields an empty list and `clearCellsUnderMerge` is never invoked for it. The other merge reads in paste (sheet.ts:2263, 2283) are likewise live. Repo-wide, `copyBuffer` appears only in sheet.ts plus `clearCopyBuffer()` calls in the views, so no alternate copy path stores a merge snapshot either.
